theme.title: Five on the Floor
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many points did Michael Jordan score in Game 6 of the 1998 Finals, the night of his title-winning last shot?
questions.note: 45, capped by the game-winner over Bryon Russell.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jordan scored 45 points, and hit a memorable game-winning shot over Jazz forward Bryon Russell

funFacts.text: Scottie Pippen aggravated his back injury on the opening dunk of the title clincher.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: aggravated his injury when he dunked the opening basket of the game

funFacts.text: Karl Malone led Utah with 31 points but could not prevent Chicago's final title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Pts: Karl Malone 31

funFacts.text: Jordan stripped the ball from Malone before setting up his winning jumper over Bryon Russell.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: When John Stockton passed the ball to Karl Malone, Jordan stole the ball away

questions.prompt: The 1971–72 Lakers set a regular-season wins record. What was their win total?
questions.note: 69–13, a record that stood until the 1995–96 Bulls.

funFacts.text: The defending champion Bucks, led by Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, were expected to own the league for years.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The defending champion Milwaukee Bucks, led by superstar Kareem Abdul-Jabbar

funFacts.text: Los Angeles swept Chicago in the conference semifinals before battling Milwaukee in the West finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Western Conference Semifinals: 4–0

funFacts.text: Boston had repeatedly denied the Lakers a championship after their move west, making this title particularly cathartic.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Lakers lost the championship to them six times in eight years

questions.prompt: The 2011–12 Bobcats closed the season on a losing streak that wasn’t snapped until the next season began. How long was it?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: embarking on a 23-game losing streak that lasted until the start of the following season.

funFacts.text: Charlotte's last victory before the drought came against Toronto in mid-March.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: On March 17, 2012, the Bobcats had their final win of the season against the Toronto Raptors

funFacts.text: The season ended with a 104–84 defeat against the New York Knicks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: losing 104–84 to the New York Knicks in their final regular season game

funFacts.text: Bismack Biyombo led Charlotte in rebounds, while D. J. Augustin led in assists.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bismack Biyombo led in rebounds per game (5.8), and point guard D. J. Augustin

questions.prompt: How many assists per game did Avery Johnson average in the 1999 Finals?
questions.note: 7.2 assists per game, plus a defining Finals shot.

funFacts.text: Johnson delivered the series-winning shot in Game 5 as the Spurs won their first title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Avery Johnson hit the game-winner

funFacts.text: Johnson led San Antonio with nine assists in the deciding game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Asts: Avery Johnson 9

funFacts.text: Johnson scored 9.2 points per game while handling the Spurs' offense during the Finals.

questions.prompt: What percentage of threes did Bryn Forbes make for the champion Bucks?
questions.note: 45.2%, a key source of floor spacing for Milwaukee.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.derivation: Source records .452 three-point accuracy; multiply by 100 for 45.2 percent.

funFacts.text: Forbes played 70 regular-season games but started only ten.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bryn Forbes | 70 | 10 | 19.3

funFacts.text: Milwaukee signed Forbes from the San Antonio Spurs in free agency.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bryn Forbes | November 26 | San Antonio Spurs

funFacts.text: His three-point accuracy dropped during the title-winning playoffs.
